findings.detail: H2.4 says cellular iron homeostasis leads to RLS with positive polarity while the mechanism says iron deficiency drives RLS; the deficiency sits only in the step's context (disease_state), so the ACO1 arm composes to ACO1 raising RLS risk against the title's direction

H3.3 says synaptic differentiation leads to RLS with positive polarity while the title says the risk variants impair it, so the arm composes to the risk alleles lowering RLS risk; the step's note ('Altered synaptic differentiation') has no direction at all

the only link from BTBD9 to ACO1 is a binds step with unknown polarity, so nothing says how the BTBD9 risk alleles change ACO1 or iron homeostasis and the BTBD9 claim has no route; the falsification test (expected negative for iron homeostasis) assumes a direction the chain never states

all three 'risk alleles decrease the gene' steps cite only GWAS rows (allele to RLS) and Open Targets scores; no cited text reports any effect of an RLS allele on MEIS1, BTBD9 or PTPRD amount, so the decreasing direction is the agent's assumption

the run's strongest evidence, six GWAS rows giving the risk allele and its direction for RLS (e.g. rs113851554-T, p = 1e-1371), states allele-to-disease links that no step makes; the run spent it on allele-to-expression steps it does not support

PMID:42309051 links abnormal cerebellar output to zebrafish locomotor defects and likens it to ataxia and dystonia; it does not say cerebellar output causes RLS, so the final MEIS1 step into the disease has no support
AGR:MGI:104717:MP:0020478 (Meis1 mutant, abnormal circadian sleep/wake cycle) is cited for both cerebellar-output steps; sleep/wake is a node of the title and the H1.2 note but of no step
the title concludes 'disrupting circadian sleep/wake cycles', but no step reaches sleep/wake; the chain jumps from cerebellar output to RLS
the title concludes 'disrupting motor circuits', but no step reaches motor circuits; the chain jumps from synaptic differentiation to RLS
two general reviews (PMID:30363981, PMID:42462324) are cited for BTBD9 binding ACO1 and for ACO1 in iron homeostasis; neither abstract names BTBD9 or ACO1

the iron-to-RLS step cites reviews that give only an undirected 'link' and 'abnormalities in brain iron metabolism', one adding that iron's role 'is still a matter of debate', and a Btbd9 mouse record with no iron in it

AGR:MGI:1916625:MP:0011396 is a Purkinje-cell (Pcp2-cre) Btbd9 knockout with abnormal sleep behavior: a cerebellar result like the MEIS1 hypothesis, cited for the brain-iron step it says nothing about

PMID:40561837 is ADHD-RLS genetic pleiotropy with a pathway annotation (synaptic plasticity, neural development) and AGR:MGI:97812:MP:0010053 is decreased grip strength in Ptprd mutant mice; neither says synaptic differentiation affects RLS

all three hypotheses are 'high' confidence and 'grounded', yet 4 of 23 citations state their step, no step into RLS has a single supporting citation, and of the four claims two compose to the opposite sign, one (BTBD9) has no route, and the one that agrees (MEIS1) has belief 0; no hypothesis lists contradicting evidence

'restless legs syndrome risk alleles' is one ungrounded label for three different loci and names no allele, though the run's own GWAS rows name them (rs113851554-T, rs2300478-G, rs10947738-A, rs61192259-A, rs34602324-G, rs1836229-A)

every node other than the genes and RLS (MONDO:0005391) has an empty curie, even 'cellular iron homeostasis', an exact GO synonym of GO:0006879; 'trans-synaptic neuronal differentiation' mixes neuron differentiation with UniProt's synaptic differentiation and was grounded here as synapse assembly (GO:0007416)

the step's context field holds 'iron deficiency' as a disease state, which reads as the state of the subject (loss of iron homeostasis) rather than a background, and it is what carries the direction the polarity field gets wrong

the only kept support for MEIS1 inhibiting cerebellar output is zebrafish meis1b (one of two zebrafish MEIS1 paralogs), and for PTPRD inducing synaptic differentiation a UniProt function inferred from mouse (ECO:0000250, Q64487)

the abstention for GLIPR1 and GABARAPL2 cites GWAS:GLIPR1:no-association, GWAS:GABARAPL2:no-association and two HPA ids that are not in sources.json, so its claims (no GWAS hit, no brain enrichment, no interaction with the RLS genes) cannot be checked against any text
BLN:CerebellarOutput: no GO, MP, HP or UBERON term names the output activity of the cerebellum, which the MEIS1 chain turns on
BLN:MEIS1-RLSRiskAlleles, BLN:BTBD9-RLSRiskAlleles, BLN:PTPRD-RLSRiskAlleles: a locus's unnamed set of RLS risk alleles has no ID, so each is a BLN variant class as the guide prescribes

a variant-to-disease association that the run cites but states at no step (here six signed GWAS rows) has nowhere to go: bridges are allowed only when an arm needs one to compose, so the H1 arm composes with no evidence on two of its three statements while signed GWAS evidence for its claim sits excluded

a binding step that changes the partner's activity in an unknown direction (BTBD9 binds ACO1) can only be a rel, which never composes, so any hypothesis whose mechanism passes through a protein interaction gets no route

a run context that names the subject's state ('iron deficiency' on a 'cellular iron homeostasis' step) fits neither a condition refinement (a background) nor the loss-of-function inversion (which reads the subject label); it was dropped and recorded in sign_note

the falsification knocks down PTPRD and says 'a failure to observe deficient synaptic differentiation would falsify the mechanism', yet sets expected to 'positive' (an increase); H1 and H2 use the field for the readout's direction (MEIS1 knockout raises cerebellar output: positive; BTBD9 knockdown lowers iron homeostasis: negative), and H3.2 has PTPRD activating the readout

the title makes BTBD9 the agent ('BTBD9 disrupts ACO1-mediated neuronal iron homeostasis'), which gives BTBD9 itself a harmful sign, while H2.1 has the risk alleles lowering BTBD9 and the mechanism blames 'Disruptions in BTBD9', a protective sign; the claims follow the chain and mechanism

S5 (BTBD9 binds ACO1) is 'established' (b 4/5) on one STRING edge with experimental 0.41 and combined 0.45, while S2 (MEIS1 inhibits cerebellar output), backed by an in vivo zebrafish mutant study, stays 'unsupported' at b 7/10

run.json H3 falsification: knockdown of PTPRD, readout trans-synaptic neuronal differentiation, expected 'positive', while its description expects 'deficient synaptic differentiation'; the curator read the same field as a direction for H2 but did not check H3

the title 'BTBD9 disrupts ACO1-mediated neuronal iron homeostasis' makes BTBD9 harmful, but H2.1 (risk alleles decrease BTBD9) and the mechanism ('Disruptions in BTBD9 alter ACO1-mediated regulation') make loss of BTBD9 harmful; the curator took the ACO1 sign from this title without noting that it reads the other way for BTBD9
